title: 2026-09-23-retrofitting-search-with-embeddings-hosting-options-discovery
summary: Early discovery for replacing parts of ArcadiaSearch's lexical ranker with embedding-based recall + rerank. Customer evaluating hosted vs dedicated vs private (VPC) deployments; throughput and per-query cost for reranking are the top concerns. They want a pilot with 100k qps equivalent load simulation and clear success criteria for latency and MRR improvement.
topics: current search stack and pain points
rerank options: bi-encoder candidate recall vs cross-encoder rerank cost
hosting choices: hosted api vs dedicated gpu pool vs private VPC
security: SOC2, SSO, KMS, data residency
action_items: Alex Morgan: Share pricing bands for hosted vs dedicated vs private and cost model example (due: 2026-09-29)
Priya Nair: Upload sample benchmark script and 1GB synthetic dataset to shared folder (due: 2026-09-27)
Jordan Lee: Provide sample query distribution (p95 length, QPS pattern) and current recall topk config (due: 2026-09-25)
next_steps: Schedule pilot kickoff (engineers + SE) week of 2026-09-28
Redwood to run initial 10k synthetic qps smoke test and share latency/cost numbers
Customer to review SOC2 + security pack and confirm VPC timeline
transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-09-23 16:00 PT
Duration: 54m
Attendees: Alex Morgan (Redwood AE), Priya Nair (Redwood SE), Luis Ortega (Redwood CS), Sam Caldwell (ArcadiaSearch CTO), Jordan Lee (Eng Lead), Maya Patel (SRE), Evan Brooks (Product)

Auto-summary (auto-gen, may be imperfect): discuss embedding path for recall and rerank, tradeoffs between cross-encoder costs and bi-encoder recall, hosting options incl VPC, sample pilot requirements.

00:00 Alex (AE): Hey everyone, thanks for joining. Quick intro from our side — I'm Alex, AE, with Priya who will lead the technical pieces. Luis will handle onboarding / success. Sam, do you want to kick off with a quick overview of what you're trying to achieve?
00:14 Sam (CTO): Yeah sure, thanks. Uh so high level — Arcadia has a fairly heavy ecommerce search product, we're seeing latencies at the top of the funnel and relevance is slipping for long-tail queries. We're exploring embeddings for the recall layer and then a rerank stage, but cost is a big concern.
00:30 Jordan (Eng Lead): To add, our current stack is ES for indexing, custom logistic ranker for final scoring. We get about 4k qps peak, but peaks are spiky. We also do experiments with a lightweight neural ranker but productionizing was too expensive.
00:45 Priya (SE): Got it, thanks. A couple quick questions — what's your current topk and how big is your index?
00:52 Jordan: Topk for recall is 100, index doc count around 120 million product records, vectors are not production yet, we have some ad hoc embeddings.
01:05 Maya (SRE): Our main blocker is hosting — we can't send PII outside EU, and procurement is picky about new vendors accessing raw product data. So VPC or private deployment would be ideal from a compliance standpoint.
01:20 Alex: Makes sense. High-level options are hosted Redwood API (fastest), Dedicated pools where you get reserved GPU capacity and data isolation, or Private (VPC / on-prem) for strict compliance. Each has tradeoffs on cost and operational overhead.
01:34 Evan (Product): For success criteria we're thinking improve MRR by 8-10% and keep 95th percentile latency for search under 200ms for the user-facing path. Is that realistic?
01:46 Priya: There are two architecture patterns we commonly see: 1) Hybrid recall where you run a fast approximate vector fanout on a vector DB (Milvus/Pinecone/ES vector), retrieve, then run a cross-encoder rerank in Redwood; or 2) Push more into Redwood where we host embeddings and do both recall and rerank in the runtime to avoid cross-system fanout. The latter reduces complexity at the cost of compute.
02:10 Sam: What's the cost delta? I mean, a cross-encoder at topk=100 sounds prohibitive.
02:18 Priya: Right — rough back-of-envelope: if you run a cross-encoder at topk=100 and qps 4k, that's 400k cross-encoder evals per second-ish if you naively scale — actually per minute, sorry, I misspoke — but it balloons. Typical pattern is: use bi-encoder (cheap) for recall topk 200, then cross-encoder rerank topk 10. That reduces rerank volume by ~20x.
02:43 Jordan: So topk math — if we do bi-encoder recall with 200 and cross-encoder top10, what's our expected latency?
02:51 Priya: Depends on model size and hosting. With a moderately sized cross (eg distil-cross or a 220M cross), with optimized batching on Redwood Dedicated you see tail latencies in the 60-120ms per document batch depending on batch size and KV cache hits. If you need a large cross (1B+), latency and cost increase.
03:16 Sam: KV cache? we heard about a "K V cash" earlier in the docs — can you explain?
03:23 Priya: Sorry transcription — KV cache (key-value cache) refers to reusing transformer intermediate keys for autoregressive models; for cross encoders it's less relevant but for generation it's very useful. For embeddings and rerank the important caching is prefix and request-level caching for popular queries.
03:39 Maya: On data residency, does Redwood allow private control plane and customer-managed VPC? We can't have search vectors leave region.
03:46 Alex: Yes, Private mode offers a customer-managed control plane and options for regional deployment. We also have on-prem packages. We can provide SOC2 docs, SSO/SAML, and KMS integration so that keys stay in your HSM. We'll share the security pack after this call.
03:58 Evan: Great. One of our concerns is vector storage — we currently use ES with vector plugin. If we continue with ES, how does Redwood integrate?
04:08 Priya: Integration patterns: 1) Fanout to external vector DB (ES/Pinecone/Milvus) for recall, send IDs to Redwood for rerank — it's low complexity but adds network hops. 2) Push vectors into Redwood's vector store (in dedicated/private) and do recall and rerank within Redwood to reduce tail latency. 3) Hybrid: keep vectors in external DB but warm a small in-memory subset in Redwood for hot items. Each has tradeoffs on freshness, cost, and tail latency.
04:36 Jordan: Freshness is important, we update product vectors several times per hour. How does sync look?
04:42 Priya: We have incremental sync tooling and webhooks; for Dedicated we can support streaming updates with eventual consistency. For high-update workloads, hybrid or external DB with fast fanout is common.
04:55 Sam: About dims — our internal tests show 768 dims give better relevance but cost is higher. Any guidance on dim selection?
05:03 Priya: Typical tradeoff: 384 or 512 dims give good throughput/cost for general ecommerce; 768 improved semantic nuance but increases storage and compute. We suggest we run small A/B with your queries: start with 512 for recall and evaluate. We also support quantized embeddings (8-bit) to reduce memory. Note: quantization may affect nearest-neighbor quality, need evals.
05:28 Jordan: We're also worried about index shard count and latency. If we do external vector DB, we may need sharding and replica complexity.
05:36 Priya: Right, that's an ops burden on the DB side. Dedicated Redwood pools abstract that — autoscaling/replicas are managed. But Dedicated has commit costs vs hosted which is pay-as-you-go.
05:50 Sam: Can you give us an example cost model? Even rough is OK.
05:55 Alex: Yes — we'll follow up with exact bands, but rough example: hosted small-scale (dev) couple hundred USD / month; production for 4k qps with cross-encoder rerank could be tens of thousands per month if fully redundant and unoptimized; Dedicated reserved capacity reduces per-query cost significantly. We'll send a model with assumptions.
06:13 Evan: Pilot scope — we'd like Redwood to run a benchmark with our query set and 1GB sample of our catalog, simulate spiky traffic to see tail latency and cost. Is that doable?
06:22 Priya: Totally — we typically do a smoke test then a scaled pilot. We'll need your sample queries and a representative shard of product data. We can provide the benchmark harness and a shared spreadsheet for results.
06:33 Jordan: Timeline — procurement needs vendor review, that's about 3 weeks. If pilot begins in early October that's cool.
06:40 Alex: Sounds feasible. We'll line up security docs and the pilot plan.

-- Transcript noise / crosstalk and small mis-transcriptions below (keeps authenticity):
07:05 Speaker 1: "so like if we quantize the vectors does retrieval..."
07:10 Priya: "quantize-ation" haha, I said quantization, sorry for the weird mispronounce.
07:18 Maya: "what's a good topk to start with cause our QPS is spiky and we don't want to blow budget"
07:25 Priya: Usually 200 recall then 10 rerank, but we can tune.
07:30 Sam: "and latency on the cross-encoder, you said 60 to 120ms — is that p95 or p99?"
07:36 Priya: Those are p95-ish numbers for optimized dedicated pools; p99 will be higher, depends on KV hit rate and batching.
07:44 Jordan: "We use SAML and Okta, SSO integration should be smooth?"
07:48 Alex: Yes, we support SSO with SAML/Okta and fine-grained RBAC.
07:52 Evan: "Do you have examples of other retail customers who ran similar pilots?"
07:56 Luis (CS): We do, we'll share a short case study around a recent retailer who moved to hybrid recall + cross-rerank and saw ~9% MRR bump.
08:05 Sam: "Regarding data residency, how airtight is private? We need logs not leave EU for audit reasons"
08:12 Alex: In Private mode you can keep control plane and audit logs in your cloud region; we'll provide the architecture doc.

27:40 Priya: (technical dive) On the reranker model selection — cross-encoders give best pairwise relevance but are expensive. Alternative is a learned reranker that operates on features + bi-encoder scores to approximate cross quality at lower cost. We can prototype both in the pilot.
28:15 Jordan: For embeddings, we noticed different vendors produce different vector distributions; will Redwood standardize or do you just pass through?
28:25 Priya: We can host multiple embedding models; we treat embeddings as first-class artifacts. For production we recommend a single canonical embed model for consistency. We can also run an embedding alignment eval during the pilot.
31:10 Sam: One blocker is procurement security attestation, will you sign our DPA and support penetration testing?
31:18 Alex: Yes, DPA standard is fine; we have penetration testing certificates and we support customer-initiated pentests under NDA. We'll send the legal pack.
34:00 Evan: If we pick Dedicated, what kind of autoscaling / burst options exist?
34:08 Priya: Dedicated gives autoscaling policies; you can configure baseline reserved and burst to public capacity. For very spiky workloads we recommend a mixed strategy: baseline Dedicated plus hosted fallback for unpredictable peaks. Redwood has policy-based routing to fail over to a lower-cost host or compatible model when dedicated is saturated.
40:12 Jordan: Is there a mechanism to measure per-route cost and attribution?
40:18 Luis: In the Console we expose token-level/call-level cost, plus per-model and per-route dashboards and traces. You can set alerts for cost regression.
42:00 Sam: Ok to recap — items I heard: Redwood to share SOC2 pack and private deployment architecture, Redwood to provide sample benchmark harness and pricing bands, Arcadia to share sample queries and 1GB data slice. Pilot kickoff week of Sep 28.
42:20 Alex: Yes, that's correct. Anything else?
42:25 Maya: One ask — can you include an example of quantized embedding storage impact on recall quality?
42:30 Priya: We'll include a short note and suggestion for eval metrics (MRR, recall@k, latency).
42:38 Evan: Cool. Thanks everyone, we'll reconvene after the security review.

Transcript end.
